title: Escalating Cyber Threats Targeting U.S. Critical Infrastructure
description:
Recent cyberattacks attributed to Iran-linked hackers have targeted water utilities in at least 12 U.S. states, highlighting vulnerabilities in operational technology (OT) systems. Experts at the Black Hat 2026 conference noted a shift from ransomware to destructive attacks, with malware capable of disabling safety systems. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has raised alarms about the potential for such attacks to compromise essential services. The U.S. government is now emphasizing resilience in cybersecurity, urging organizations to prepare for operational continuity amid increasing threats. The CI Fortify program aims to enhance readiness for downtime and offline operations in critical sectors. The trend of destructive attacks reflects a growing willingness among hackers to cause significant damage rather than merely disrupt services.

Key Points:
• Iran-linked hackers have attacked water utilities in at least 12 U.S. states.
• Cybersecurity experts warn of a shift from ransomware to destructive malware targeting OT systems.
• The U.S. government is emphasizing resilience and continuity in critical infrastructure cybersecurity.
